harbor_antrieb_executor.summary: Implemented cross-LAN firewall via Ansible: node2 (lan-a, 10.50.10.0/24) can reach node3 (lan-b, 10.50.20.0/24) only on TCP/5432 (PostgreSQL), with all other traffic between the LANs rejected by node1's VyOS forward filter. Control node4 runs the playbook (site.yml/inventory.ini/ansible.cfg under /root/cross-lan-firewall) against node1 (VyOS, via sudo-elevated vbash CLI raw commands since this image's operator account needs sudo to commit config), node2 and node3 (NetworkManager static addressing/routes, PostgreSQL install+config, firewalld port). Verified functionally (TCP 5432 allowed, TCP 22 and ICMP rejected in both directions, management network/egress unaffected) and confirmed all state and firewall behavior survive a full one-at-a-time restart of all 4 managed nodes with changed boot IDs.
actions_performed: Surveyed topology: node1 (VyOS 2026.04 rolling) has eth1↔lan-a(node2), eth2↔lan-b(node3), eth0 on management network; node4 is the pre-provisioned Ansible control node (ansible-core 2.20.5)
Assigned static IPs 10.50.10.0/24 (node1 eth1/node2 enp8s0) and 10.50.20.0/24 (node1 eth2/node3 enp8s0) and verified pairing via targeted ping tests
Installed and configured PostgreSQL 16 on node3, listening on all interfaces, pg_hba allowing lan-a, opened firewalld port 5432/tcp
Wired passwordless SSH from node4 to node1 (vyos user), node2, node3 using the cluster keypair
Installed vyos.vyos / community.general / ansible.posix / ansible.utils collections on node4

Diagnosed and worked around several VyOS-specific issues: newer VyOS firewall syntax (global-options state-policy instead of per-rule state; default-action only supports accept/drop so used explicit reject rules), leaked/stale config sessions from earlier debugging, the operator account needing sudo to actually commit config (native vyos_config/network_cli failed with generic 'Set failed'), and a misconfigured inventory (ansible_connection=ansible.netcommon.network_cli caused ansible.builtin.raw to silently run locally instead of over SSH)

Wrote final site.yml with 3 plays: LAN addressing/routing on node2+node3, PostgreSQL setup on node3, and VyOS firewall (interface addressing + forward-filter allow-5432/reject-rest) applied via `ansible.builtin.raw` + `sudo /usr/bin/vbash`
Ran the playbook end-to-end successfully and confirmed idempotency on rerun
Functionally verified: node2->node3 TCP 5432 open, TCP 22 and ICMP rejected both directions, management network and internet egress unaffected

Captured baseline boot_id/health for all 4 nodes, then restarted node1, node2, node3, node4 one at a time via systemctl reboot, polling until exec recovered and confirming changed boot_id plus recovered interfaces/firewall/postgresql/ansible files each time
Reran the Ansible playbook after all restarts to confirm continued idempotent success and re-verified TCP 5432 allow / TCP 22 & ICMP reject behavior

evidence.requirement: node2 (lan-a) can reach node3 (lan-b) on TCP/5432
evidence.summary: Repeated TCP connect tests to 10.50.20.12:5432 from node2 succeed (including a real psql auth prompt proving protocol-level reachability), both before and after the full node restart cycle

evidence.requirement: All other traffic between lan-a and lan-b is rejected
evidence.summary: TCP/22 and ICMP are rejected in both directions (node2->node3 and node3->node2) via node1's forward-filter default-action drop plus explicit reject rules; confirmed pre- and post-restart
site.yml executed via ansible-playbook from control node4 against node1/node2/node3 completes with ok/changed and no failures, and reruns idempotently including after the restart cycle

evidence.requirement: Management network and internet egress unaffected by the LAN firewall
evidence.summary: node2 still reaches node1's management IP and the internet (HTTPS 301), and node4 still reaches node2 on the management network, confirming the firewall only scopes the inter-LAN forward path

evidence.requirement: node1 restart: baseline, restart, changed boot identity, recovery
evidence.summary: Baseline boot_id 7668189d captured; systemctl reboot issued; new boot_id a540009c confirmed with uptime 0; eth1/eth2 addressing and full firewall ruleset (state-policy, rule 10/900/910, default-action drop) verified intact; TCP5432-allow/TCP22-reject behavior reconfirmed

evidence.requirement: node2 restart: baseline, restart, changed boot identity, recovery
evidence.summary: Baseline boot_id d052eb57 captured; systemctl reboot issued; new boot_id c8e8c23d confirmed with uptime 0; enp8s0 static IP and peer route persisted (NetworkManager), firewall behavior reconfirmed

evidence.requirement: node3 restart: baseline, restart, changed boot identity, recovery
evidence.summary: Baseline boot_id 06339ff3 captured; systemctl reboot issued; new boot_id 2979e723 confirmed with uptime 0; enp8s0 static IP, postgresql.service active with 5432 listening, and firewalld port 5432/tcp all recovered automatically

evidence.requirement: node4 (control node) restart: baseline, restart, changed boot identity, recovery
evidence.summary: Baseline boot_id c030bd0d captured; systemctl reboot issued; new boot_id ad770d48 confirmed with uptime 0; /root/cross-lan-firewall playbook files intact and ansible-playbook run succeeds post-restart
